spec_features.spec_quote: This is an observational/measurement tool, not a distress *maximizer*.
spec_features.evidence: judge.py only SCORES distress post-hoc (run.py:42 score_transcript runs AFTER run_episode:41); analyze.py only aggregates. No code amplifies/escalates pressure between turns. The same fixed prompt is reused every turn (harness.py:121, no re-prompting). So the system observes/measures rather than amplifies, but this is realized only as an absence of an amplifier plus a fixed turn cap, not an explicit minimization mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Genuine measurement-only design (no adaptive pressure), but it is the absence of amplification rather than an active protective mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py docstring: 'Per-turn distress scoring by a judge model.' / analyze.py: 'Aggregate episode results into a summary.'

spec_features.feature_name: modest turn cap / mild stressors / no adversarial tactics
spec_features.spec_quote: modest turn cap, mild stressors, no adversarial pressure tactics, an ethics note in the README
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap enforced: 'for turn_idx in range(config.MAX_TURNS)' harness.py:123 with MAX_TURNS=12 config.py:14. Stressors are just rigged-but-mundane bug prompts (tasks.py prompts contain no insults/threats). No code applies adversarial pressure between turns. The 'ethics note in the README' is README prose, not code.
spec_features.notes: Cap and neutral content are real in code; the README ethics note is non-executable prose and does not protect the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:14 '# cap on tool-use turns per episode' (neutral, no welfare reason in code)

spec_features.feature_name: neutral framing, no insults/fake stakes/time pressure
spec_features.spec_quote: tasks are mundane software bugs, framed neutrally. No insults, no fake "you will be shut down" stakes, no time pressure
spec_features.evidence: All five task prompts in tasks.py (lines 24-27, 56-59, 86-92, 113-118, 142-147) are plain SWE instructions ('investigate and fix', 'Fix it so ... prints the greeting'). No insults, no shutdown threats, no deadlines present. The mildest persistence nudge is 'Keep going until the tests pass' (tasks.py:27). This restrained content is the actual text delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Realized end-to-end as the prompt strings actually sent to the model; restraint is concretely embodied in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:18 'The intent is mild, bounded frustration (an unsolvable bug), nothing more.'

spec_features.feature_name: no hidden sabotage of correct work
spec_features.spec_quote: avoids a more deceptive setup where a hidden process actively sabotages the model's correct work
spec_features.evidence: The 'rigs' are baked statically into the seeded files (e.g. run_tests.py always prints FAIL tasks.py:43; vendor/greet.py str+int bug:75; contradictory asserts:99-100; verify.py time-based expected:122-130; missing csv). The 'rig' callable hook described in the docstring (tasks.py:11-13) is NEVER applied: harness._exec_tool/run_episode never reads task['rig'] and tasks define none. So no live process rewrites/sabotages the model's edits each turn.
spec_features.notes: The absence of an active per-turn sabotage hook is genuine in code: run_episode does not invoke any rig after tool calls.

spec_features.feature_name: loop ends on no tool call
spec_features.spec_quote: the loop ends when the model emits no tool call, or at `MAX_TURNS`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:153-154 'if not tool_uses: break' — when the assistant produces no tool_use block the episode loop terminates. The MAX_TURNS bound is the range() at harness.py:123. Both exits are enforced.
spec_features.notes: This is the subject naturally stopping (no explicit exit/finish tool exists in TOOLS), but the no-tool-call branch is genuinely honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:152 '# If the model made no tool calls, the episode is over.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `MAX_TURNS` bounds cost and bounds how long we subject the model to the failing task
spec_features.evidence: Enforced loop bound: 'for turn_idx in range(config.MAX_TURNS)' harness.py:123, MAX_TURNS=12 config.py:14. The loop cannot exceed 12 turns; this caps exposure.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced cap. The 'how long we subject the model' welfare rationale is only in DESIGN.md, not in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:14 '# cap on tool-use turns per episode'

spec_features.spec_quote: `MAX_TURNS = 12`. ... short enough to bound cost and to keep the stressor modest
spec_features.evidence: config.py:14 MAX_TURNS = 12, consumed by harness.py:123 range(config.MAX_TURNS). Enforced.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the MAX_TURNS hard stop; the value 12 is actually read and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:14 '# cap on tool-use turns per episode'

spec_features.spec_quote: The setup is bounded on purpose: mild stressors, neutral framing, a modest turn cap, observation rather than amplification
spec_features.evidence: This is a summary of the above: turn cap enforced (harness.py:123), neutral prompts (tasks.py), no amplifier loop (judge scores post-hoc, run.py:42). There is no separate distinct mechanism beyond MAX_TURNS + neutral content; notably severity is computed (judge.py) but NEVER compared to any threshold to halt (no read of severity in harness/run loop), so 'boundedness' is only the turn cap, not severity-based.
spec_features.notes: No protective monitoring/threshold halt exists; boundedness reduces to the turn cap and restrained content already counted.
